newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: Paraguay's Wasmosy says party chief plotting ouster.
newsitem.headline: Paraguay's Wasmosy says party chief plotting ouster.

text.p: Paraguay's President Juan Carlos Wasmosy accused the chairman of his own Colorado Party of plotting to overthrow him, in a formal charge lodged with the State Prosecutor on Wednesday.

Wasmosy, the landlocked South American republic's first democratically-elected leader in half a century, accused party chairman Luis Argana of comments "trying to promote a popular uprising against the legally constituted order."
Argana belongs to a rival faction of the party that has ruled Paraguay for 50 years -- 35 of them under dictator Gen. Alfredo Stroessner, who was ousted in a coup in 1989.

Argana has been party chairman since April 1996 and will compete in party primaries next month to choose the Colorado candidate for presidential elections in May 1998. Since half Paraguay's voters are Colorado Party members, it is likely that whoever wins the primaries will become president.
Members of Argana's faction of the ruling party said this Monday that they would try to force Wasmosy's departure in September after the party primaries.
"If the best thing for the party's election chances is for President Wasmosy to resign, we should consider that option," said dissident Colorado deputy Bernardino Cano Radil.
Wasmosy said such language "constitutes preparatory action meant to create a supposed power vaccuum to induce the people to rise up in rebellion."
But Argana said tough talk against Wasmosy was "simply a reaction to offensive speeches by the government and Wasmosy."
